props.title: 3D lab: your spacecraft and the satellite in orbit around the Earth

requirements.instruction: The satellite is 51 km ahead. Catch it in one lap.
Same gap, with 2.5 m/s of fuel for both burns. Take up to three laps.
Now the satellite is 34 km behind you. Let it catch up within two laps.

props.textAlternative:
**Text version of the lab.** Your spacecraft and a satellite fly the same circular orbit, 500 km up. For each rendezvous you choose a burn, from braking 5 m/s to speeding up 5 m/s in steps of 0.5 m/s, and, when the rendezvous allows it, a number of laps. Your spacecraft burns, flies its laps, then burns the same amount the other way at the same point: both burns use fuel. The rendezvous is caught when the satellite is within 2 km at the end. At 500 km, each m/s of braking gains about 17 km per lap.

1. The satellite is 51 km ahead. Catch it in one lap.
2. Same gap, with 2.5 m/s of fuel for both burns. Take up to three laps.
3. Now the satellite is 34 km behind you. Let it catch up within two laps, with 2.5 m/s of fuel.

events.description: Open the debrief once the three rendezvous are caught.

props.markdown: The same 51 km took 6 m/s of fuel in one lap, and 2 m/s in three. That is why real rendezvous take their time: hours, sometimes days.
